text:
Anya: Pinging design crew I made a super-compact layout for the notify preview (goal: fit 8 channels in one view). Quick accessibility pass please? :mag:

Lucy: Shared the Figma link in thread. First glance: when pills wrap, keyboard focus follows source DOM order which doesn't match visual flow. That confuses tabbing.

Jon: Can we avoid CSS-only reordering? Flex-wrap is the culprit; visual wrap != DOM order. Two options: reorder DOM to match visual grid, or use grid with consistent ordering. Grid worked for me but broke name truncation.

Priyanka: Truncation is important for long translations (e.g., German). Proposal: truncate with "..." and expose full label via tooltip + aria-describedby on focus. SR should read the expanded form.

Anya: Good. Also copy check: action says "Mute channel" in current mock. Product prefers "Snooze notifications". We'll standardize to "Snooze" across all previews.

Lucy: A11y note: each pill needs role="button" and aria-pressed for active suppression. If a channel is suppressed by routing rules (not just toggled), aria-label should reflect that: e.g., "Slack - suppressed by route (quiet window)".

Priyanka: Regarding announcements: when a user snoozes from the preview, we should fire a polite live region: "Snoozed Slack for 2 hours". Avoid repeating multiple live messages when virtualizing the list. Batch updates if many changes.

Jon: Implementation detail: virtualization + live regions are tricky. If we recycle DOM nodes, SR may announce stale content. Strategy: keep a short-term hidden live region dedicated to user actions (not to list render).

Anya: Visual hint idea: a low-contrast badge icon indicates "will receive" vs "won't receive" given routing rules. For sighted users it's helpful. For SR, include an offscreen label like "Preview result: Email only".

Lucy: Contrast problem: our pill foreground uses 13px/500 with 60% white on dark bg. Fails 4.5:1. Options: increase font weight to 600, darken text color, or add 1px outline. I prefer darkening text to preserve layout.

Priyanka: Also keyboard flow: open suppression drawer -> focus should land on first control (duration). On close (esc or done) return focus to originating pill. Add focus-trap in the drawer.

Anya: Will add that to the interaction spec. Also, small UX decision: when a pill is disabled because of route priority, should the toggle be interactive? I think show disabled toggle with tooltip explaining why ("This channel is lower priority and won't get alerts for this rule").

Jon: Agree. Disabled + explanatory tooltip is best. Dev note: use aria-disabled="true" and provide an explanation element referenced by aria-describedby.

a11y-bot: Checklist: ensure logical DOM order matches visual order, role and aria-pressed on pills, aria-label includes channel + status, aria-live for user actions only, focus management for drawer, contrast >= 4.5:1, run axe + NVDA manual pass.
